hook.text: Hendrix lost the side one master tape in a London taxi, and most of that side was remixed in one overnight session.

facts.label: Recorded
facts.value: May to June, October 1967, at Olympic Studios, London

facts.label: Players
facts.value: Jimi Hendrix (vocals, electric guitar, piano, recorder), Noel Redding (bass guitars, backing vocals), Mitch Mitchell (drums, backing vocals)

sentences.text: The Jimi Hendrix Experience finished its debut, Are You Experienced, at the end of April 1967 and kept up a regular schedule of recording sessions.
On May 4 the band was back at Olympic Studios in London and began writing songs for its next LP.
The new record came out only seven months after that debut.
Eddie Kramer was the engineer, with George Chkiantz as second engineer.
The band cut basic tracks on a four-track machine: drums in stereo on two channels, bass on a third, and Hendrix's rhythm guitar on the fourth.
Those were mixed down to two tracks on a second four-track machine, leaving two free for things like lead guitar, vocals and extra percussion.
Kramer stayed patient with Hendrix, who often asked for many retakes.
By October 1967 Chas Chandler was tired of Hendrix's perfectionism, and Noel Redding began to resent Hendrix's instructions on what he played.
In 2010 the posthumous album West Coast Seattle Boy: The Jimi Hendrix Anthology included "Cat Talking to Me", a song recorded in the June sessions but left off the album.
On November 7, 2025 the Hendrix Estate released a box set called The Jimi Hendrix Experience: Bold As Love Sessions, with 66 tracks of demos and alternate takes.
Some Hindus have since been angry about the religious images on the cover, and Malaysia's Home Ministry banned the album's art after complaints.

listen_for.text: Microphonic and harmonic feedback run through the track, and the guitar sounds move across the stereo image, circling the listener.
Hendrix runs his guitar through a Leslie speaker here for the first time, a revolving speaker that gives a wavering sound.
Hendrix plays a recorder on it, and the percussion effect comes from Chas Chandler, Hendrix, Graham Nash and Gary Leeds stamping their feet on a drum riser.
The chorus is built on tremolo-picked partial chords, and the coda has stereo phasing.
The lyrics were inspired by The Spanish Castle, a dance hall near Seattle where Hendrix played with local bands as a high school student.
